name: Redline Armory Conceal Vest
description:
A close-fitting vest in matte dark olive, cut to look like a casual utility vest from the outside — four visible exterior pockets with zip closures, a mock-suede panel at the shoulders, a full zip front. Inside is a different story: four internal holster positions (two shoulder, two hip-flank), each with adjustable retention straps and magnetic quick-release. The inner lining is a ballistic-resistant soft panel rated for standard kinetic rounds — not full armor, but enough to make a difference at range. The exterior fabric is a tightly woven synthetic that doesn't print.

Redline Armory is a licensed civilian arms and accessories manufacturer operating in the grey zone between Tier 3 and 4 markets. The Conceal Vest is their civilian carry flagship — legal in most corponation jurisdictions with proper registration, and popular with private security contractors, off-duty enforcement personnel, and Tier 3 residents in neighborhoods where the threat assessment justifies it. It's also, quietly, popular with people who are not licensed and don't intend to be.
functionality: Internal ballistic soft armor rated for standard kinetic rounds at range. Four concealed holster positions with adjustable magnetic retention. Does not print through exterior fabric.
what_it_says: You carry, or you want people to think you do, or you're worried enough about something specific that you spent the money.
story_hooks: A run of the 2198 production batch had a manufacturing defect in the ballistic panel — a void in the material that only covers a 4cm area over the left side. Redline hasn't issued a recall.
The vest's magnetic retention hardware can be remotely triggered by a specific EM frequency — a vulnerability that someone has weaponized.
A Tier 1 resident has somehow acquired a Redline Conceal Vest; the question is whether they bought it, stole it, or were given it — and by whom.

physical_description.visual_profile: A deceptively casual utility vest that reads as streetwear at first glance—structured but not overtly tactical. The matte olive colorway and relaxed exterior pocket placement make it blend into Tier 3 urban wear. The mock-suede shoulder panels add a subtle designer touch that keeps it from looking purely functional. On a body, it sits between the chest and hips with a clean vertical line, neither bulky nor slim.
physical_description.fit: Close-fitting through the torso without compression; allows free shoulder movement. Cut to prevent printing or showing the weight of internal systems. Armholes are generous enough for layering or accessing side holsters. Length hits mid-hip.
physical_description.primary_material: Exterior: tightly woven synthetic ballistic composite (proprietary Redline weave, non-reflective). Mock-suede accent panels at shoulders (treated polymer). Interior lining: soft ballistic-resistant panel rated for standard kinetic rounds (polyester/aramid blend).
physical_description.texture: Exterior feels smooth and dense to the touch, almost leatherlike in matte finish. Mock-suede shoulders have subtle nap. Interior lining is slightly tacky, designed to grip and stabilize holstered items. All seams are professionally finished but visible.
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte dark olive as primary (borrows from military heritage but desaturated for civilian wear). Black reinforcement stitching throughout. Interior lining dark charcoal. Zipper hardware: gunmetal grey with subtle Redline branding on pulls.
physical_description.closures: Full-length YKK zipper down center front with dual pulls. Four exterior pockets secured by heavy-duty friction-fit zips. Internal holster straps use adjustable velcro retention with magnetic quick-release hardware (silent deployment).
distinctive_features: Four visible exterior utility pockets (no visible internal holster hints from outside)
Mock-suede shoulder panels (aesthetic/functional—reduced glare on skin during draw)
Ballistic-resistant soft-panel lining (marked with faint Redline Armory QR code for registration verification)
Four internal holster positions: two shoulder mounts, two hip-flank mounts with adjustable retention
Magnetic quick-release system (barely audible—purpose is plausible deniability)
Concealed interior document pocket (registration papers, permit copy)
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3–4 crossover. Licensed civilians and private security wear openly; Tier 5 residents wear to avoid attention but signal capability.
physical_description.cultural_context: Wearer is armed, regulated or not. Projects quiet competence and threat awareness. Popular with off-duty enforcement, private contractors, and people who believe their neighborhood requires self-sufficiency. Wearing it signals either legal authorization or calculated risk.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine to broken-in. High-end units show minimal wear (occasional holster scuffing on interior). Street units often show shoulder seam stress, zipper patina, and subtle creasing from repeated access. Older models may have velcro pilling.
